back: Spread by contaminated water, usually from human waste: cholera, typhoid, dysentery.
Carried by a living carrier: malaria (Anopheles mosquito), sleeping sickness (tsetse fly).
Caused by a poor diet: kwashiorkor (protein), marasmus (energy), pellagra (niacin).
Non-communicable disease linked to diet, inactivity, smoking, alcohol and ageing: heart disease, type 2 diabetes, cancers.
Highest risk in hot, low-lying areas (Zambezi valley, Lowveld, border valleys) in the hot wet season; lowest on the highveld.
Zimbabwe epidemic: roughly 100,000 cases, over 4,000 deaths (approximate); failing water and sewage systems.
Water and sanitation, climate, wealth and diet, health care, education, age structure.
Lower life expectancy, orphans, children leaving school to care, stigma, pressure on clinics.
Lost working days and skills, lower output, household spending on treatment, government health costs.
